subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should externally, plugin, or agent-created recurring cron jobs remain auto-enabled, default disabled pending operator approval, or move behind a trusted scheduling API with provenance and explicit model/cost policy?
rationale: This changes cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, doctor/update behavior, and security posture for existing automation, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Provenance-based scheduling API
options.body: Introduce a trusted scheduling path that records who created the job, requires operator approval or safe defaults for untrusted recurring jobs, and makes model/cost policy explicit.

options.title: Default external jobs disabled
options.body: Keep the existing cron API but make externally registered recurring jobs inactive until the operator enables them, with migration and doctor messaging for existing jobs.

options.title: Keep enablement and add spend guards
options.body: Preserve current auto-enable behavior but add model warnings, budget enforcement, and quota circuit breakers to reduce runaway-cost impact without changing scheduling consent.

recommendation.title: Provenance-based scheduling API
recommendation.body: Introduce a trusted scheduling path that records who created the job, requires operator approval or safe defaults for untrusted recurring jobs, and makes model/cost policy explicit.
